speakers: Katy Kaminski (AlphaSimplex, trend following researcher; caption 'Katie Kaminsky')
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Ep.356 (mid July 2025): Katy Kaminski on her paper about managed futures drawdowns and recovery, exogenous vs endogenous shocks, a non-parametric regime paper and CTA replication. Conclusions: drawdowns coincide with strong equities and recover fast in stress, rebalance rather than time trend, replicators outperformed due to slower speed and smaller sets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: CTA programs that are focused on China markets actually had somewhat of a different experience in June, doing somewhat worse than the traditional CTA programs
claims.claim: China-focused CTA programs underperformed traditional CTAs in June 2025, probably because Chinese futures are commodity heavy and geopolitical moves hit energies hard, while metals trended.
claims.indicator: China-focused CTA programs vs traditional CTAs

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: this is the largest single day price surge in records going back to 1968
claims.claim: COMEX copper rose about 13% in a day on tariff news (largest since 1968) while London and Chinese copper were unaffected, and CTAs were likely on the right side.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it shows how isolated incidents can actually directly link to trends that extend
claims.claim: Isolated tariff events can start trends: long signals in metals (copper, platinum) were building on trade tension and potential tariffs.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it just shows the diversification of the commodity sector that you know a lot of investors don't really have exposure to directly
claims.claim: The commodity sector provides diversification that most investors do not hold directly, which CTAs supply.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: also some short exposure in fixed income, US fixed income I should say, probably doing okay for for managers
claims.claim: In early July 2025 CTAs were long equities and metals and short US fixed income with some gains in livestock and grains; European fixed income was tricky.
claims.direction: Long equities, long metals, short US bonds

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the two asset classes that have actually trended the most this year has been equities recently
claims.claim: Equities and a weak dollar trended most in 2025, though the dollar had started to revert in July.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: fixed income is definitely underweighted by trend falling signals
claims.claim: Fixed income was choppy (steepening and flattening, Fed back and forth) so trend signals gave it little weight.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: energies were really tricky last month because they shocked big and then they came back down and now they're back up again
claims.claim: Energies spiked, reversed and rebounded in June-July 2025, which was hard for trend following, while metals tied to trade policy were more interesting.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: to now having to suddenly consider buying back at all-time highs I mean these are psychologically very difficult decisions to make
claims.claim: Discretionary investors who cut equities in April find it psychologically hard to buy back at record highs, while systematic managers are indifferent.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I've seen a pretty large shift in sentiment um in the last two weeks or so where the world is kind of saying actually growth looks a little better than we thought
claims.claim: Sentiment shifted in early July 2025 toward better growth with rotation into US small caps, a tentative environment for equities.
claims.indicator: growth sentiment, small vs large cap

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Stocken trend flat for the month so far, down 10% for the year
claims.claim: Mid-July 2025 CTA indices were down about 3% to 10% year to date while MSCI World was up 8.7% and S&P 500 up 5.85%.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the largest draw down was actually between 2015 and 2019
claims.claim: Among managed-futures drawdowns above 10%, the largest was 2015-2019 (Trump's first term era), and the paper plots drawdown depth, duration and recovery.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: that just shows that there's a lot of variation across different draw down periods
claims.claim: Drawdown and recovery times vary a lot, so the current drawdown could recover fast or slowly.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: equities tend to be doing very well. Um, when things are difficult for us
claims.claim: Trend drawdowns tend to occur while equities are doing very well (shown with equity returns during each SG Trend Index drawdown).

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it tends to be really challenging environments, recovery is a lot faster
claims.claim: Recoveries from trend drawdowns are faster when equities are stressed and slower when equities keep making new highs, so trend is useful in both.
claims.indicator: drawdown recovery time vs equity returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you almost get the sum of the two meaning both returns on top of each other
claims.claim: A blend of trend following and the S&P 500 gives nearly the sum of both returns (portable alpha), explaining the stream of new overlay products.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: even though people think of say fixed income as more mean reverting, it actually has an more of an inbuilt momentum
claims.claim: Per Ilmanen's paper, bonds have more inbuilt momentum while equities revert (V-shapes), so fixed income gives the best trend profits.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: trend has done very well in a falling rate environment especially when the curve is steep
claims.claim: Fixed-income trend depends on regime: strong in falling rates with a steep curve, strong short when the curve is inverted, mixed when flat as now.
claims.direction: Long bonds in falling rates with steep curve; short when inverted

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the worst two are really the uh the trade war number one which is Trump's first uh term and then now the liberation
claims.claim: The two worst trend drawdown-recovery combinations coincided with Trump trade-war periods, 2018 and 2025.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the recovery that we've seen in the S&P 500 uh, since liberation day uh, of a 20% or more draw down is the quickest recovery on record
claims.claim: The post-Liberation Day S&P recovery (57 days, no Fed support) was the fastest ever from a 20% drawdown, a V-shape that trend following is not built for.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: we were doing a a study of Trump's tweets and we just didn't find that much trends that he could trump
claims.claim: Trump 1.0 tweets did not create much trend, but Trump 2.0 coincides with larger global change in geopolitics and supply chains.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the initial shock is often bad because it's based on rhetoric and people realizing that change is coming
claims.claim: For trend, initial rhetoric-driven shocks are bad, but once fundamental data show the new direction (e.g. copper tariffs) trends emerge in asset classes.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I'm hoping for something a little bit more substantial than than a tariff
claims.claim: Tariff-driven positions (long copper) are fragile because tariffs can be reversed by the next statement.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: recoveries are often linked to kind of an real narrative change
claims.claim: Trend recoveries often follow a real narrative change in a broad range of markets, such as rates rising after the post-GFC period.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: that period before 2014 before energies um exploded
claims.claim: The 'CTA winter' (2010-2014, second longest drawdown) came after the GFC when the world recovered and ended with the 2014 energy collapse.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: CTA drawdowns are so much smaller than equity draw down
claims.claim: CTA index drawdowns of about 20% are small next to a 55% S&P 500 drawdown.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the rolling 12 months return that are less than minus5% for the CTA index
claims.claim: The Man paper shows rolling 12-month CTA returns below -5% are very rare compared to returns above +15% (about 59 vs 2-4 instances).

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the key is you shouldn't time, but you should, you know, rebalance
claims.claim: Do not time trend following; the strategy mean-reverts at long horizons, so rebalance (buy after drawdowns, trim after gains).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I see people selling trend after it's done well. I rarely see people buying trend when it's done poorly
claims.claim: Investors chase performance and rarely rebalance into trend after poor returns.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it's one of the few things that tends to on average um do well during periods of distress or challenging equity markets
claims.claim: Trend following is one of few robust equity complements that pays in distress; no better alternative has been found.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I have my you know my first responders, my second responders, my third responders
claims.claim: Institutions build layered defensive portfolios of different diversifiers, trend as one layer.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of people like to look at individual line items rather than looking at what the effect on the portfolio is doing and they use sharp for something they should never use sharp for
claims.claim: Evaluate trend by its portfolio effect, not stand-alone Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: exogenous shocks and impacts on CTO CTA performance versus indogenous so things that comes from inside the system and not from the outside
claims.claim: CFM's work separates exogenous shocks (Liberation Day tariffs) from endogenous ones (2022 rates positioning) for CTA performance.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: an exogenous shock that is not sustainable in shorter term that just is sort of a whipssaw those are the worst
claims.claim: Exogenous shocks that reverse quickly (whipsaw) are the worst for trend, but those that extend can help.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: they started buying bonds so there were some interesting trends that actually leaked out in other asset classes in COVID
claims.claim: Covid was less damaging than Liberation Day because supply chain trouble was anticipated and bonds rallied, giving trends outside equities.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the market is much more reticent to react because the change and the shock has already occurred
claims.claim: After Liberation Day, further shocks (copper tariffs) get smaller reactions; endogenous shocks (monetary policy, inflation) are more likely next.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: endogenous shocks tend to be more positive for uh trend perhaps because it's it's really a fundamental based shift in sort of how people are valuing assets
claims.claim: Endogenous shocks (policy, inflation) tend to help trend because they are fundamental valuation shifts.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we all get the news at the same time but we kind of digest it at different speeds
claims.claim: Trend works because news is digested at different speeds; a tariff is understood instantly but Covid took time, leaving time to position short energy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Short-term doing better like it should uh compared to long-term, but actually it's kind of completely reversed in the last uh couple of months
claims.claim: Short-term CTAs beat long-term in April 2025 but the order reversed in May-June.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: in liberation day it was really just you know a three-day move two or three days
claims.claim: A three-day shock followed by rebound is too short to detect statistically, unlike Covid, which lasted a month or two.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: nonparametric means that you're not sort of defining parameters to define regimes
claims.claim: A non-parametric regime approach avoids pre-defining regimes (rising or falling rates), which creates bias; critics say the seven state variables were chosen with hindsight.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: what is known as a uklidian distance measure or a measure of similarity
claims.claim: The Harvey et al. regime method standardises seven state variables (equities, yield curve shape, volatility, copper, etc.) and measures Euclidean distance of the current month to every past month.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if it did well in all those past events, we assume that regimes are somewhat persistent
claims.claim: Strategies that did well in similar past months are expected to do well next month, so one overweights trend or value accordingly.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you come up with all these huge parameter space of decisions you're very likely to fit history
claims.claim: Rule-based regime definitions overfit history, so tests must be walk-forward and account for how many variables were tried.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: I'm pretty certain um you're going to see some regime connection between trend um and certain sort of more recessionary regimes
claims.claim: Trend likely connects to recessionary regimes (e.g. inverted curve in fixed income), which the non-parametric method could test.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: replication strategies have done quite a lot better uh than uh the benchmarks they're trying to replicate
claims.claim: Replicators outperformed their benchmarks in 2025, implying either large tracking error or a separate alpha strategy.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: most of the replicator strategies out there are, you know, a little smaller in asset set. They also, um, are tending to be more slow in terms of, you know, how they move
claims.claim: Replicators are smaller in market set and slower, so they reacted less to Liberation Day shock and kept near average CTA returns.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: tracking error is kind of within range uh for for what we expect
claims.claim: Replicator tracking error in 2025 is within expected range per the paper's methodology.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: regression based is really sort of looking at the past and that is the slowest approach
claims.claim: Regression-based replication is slowest; mechanical or hybrid replication can be faster to track CTA performance.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if you were trying to trade Coco two years ago like replication cannot pick that up
claims.claim: Replicators miss markets outside their set (cocoa), so differences reflect market regimes not luck.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: you're running an a replicated replication strategy that has no European debt and only trades US, you're going to see variation where you don't capture those European moves
claims.claim: Tracking error depends on market set and implementation, so investors must understand inputs to measure it.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: it's just another strategy that can be combined with other CTAs that might smooth the overall dispersion
claims.claim: Replication can be a separate strategy combined with CTAs to reduce dispersion.
